Iskæmi (ischemia) is a severe acute surgical condition that demands urgent clinical attention. In the context of acute surgical guidelines, it is identified as a critical diagnosis where early antibiotic treatment is strongly recommended to halt the progression of infection, even if the patient does not present with a fever or altered infection markers [^src1]. Consequently, ischemia defines a specific subgroup of patients for whom the timing of antibiotic administration is particularly urgent [^src1].

Within the national quality development efforts outlined in the Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) draft from January 2026, ischemia is categorized among life-threatening acute surgical conditions, alongside severe ileus and perforated hollow organs [^src1]. The clinical recommendations dictate that antibiotics must be initiated as quickly as possible for patients suspected of suffering from these conditions [^src1]. This urgency directly supports the database's primary quality indicator, which monitors the administration of antibiotics within a strict three-hour window to ensure timely treatment and improve patient outcomes in acute surgical care.

## Mentions
- Page 12: "Det anbefales derfor at man iværksætter antibiotika hurtigst muligt på patienter mistænkt for svær ileus, perforeret hulorgan eller iskæmi, uanset om der er feber eller påvirkede infektionstal." [^src1]
